privacy.metaDesc: How AnimeLegacy stores your data and how to exercise your GDPR rights.
privacy.title: Your data, on your terms.
privacy.dataBody: When you use AnimeLegacy, the following personal data is created and tied to your account:

dataList.account: Email address and authentication record (Firebase Auth).
dataList.list: Every anime you add to your list, along with its status, progress, rating, and review.
dataList.activity: A timeline of changes you make to your list (status updates, ratings, reviews).
dataList.profile: Your username, bio, avatar (stored as a data URL inside your own user document).

privacy.storageBody: All personal data is stored in Google Firestore (Firebase) under your user ID. Anime catalogue entries and global character favourite counters are shared across users and contain no personal data. No third-party analytics or trackers are used.
privacy.rightsBody: You can at any time request:

rightsList.access: A copy of the personal data we hold about you.
rightsList.rectify: Correction of inaccurate data (most fields you can already edit in your profile).
rightsList.erase: Complete erasure of your account and all associated data.
rightsList.export: An export of your list and ratings in JSON format.

privacy.contactBody: If the self-service deletion in your profile is unavailable, send an email from the address tied to your account. Include your username. We'll confirm once the data has been removed.
privacy.slaNote: We respond within 30 days, in line with GDPR Article 17.

blurb.winter: A season for cosy commitment — quieter shows hold the centre while the late premieres find their feet.
blurb.spring: A patient season. Quieter shows are doing the heavy lifting — and a long-awaited mecha return is testing how much the genre has changed.
blurb.summer: Loud, bright, and full of risks — the season tradition lets writers swing for spectacle before autumn pulls everyone back.
blurb.fall: The year sharpens. Headline sequels meet first-time directors, and the calendar gets unusually crowded for a few short weeks.

editorial.winter: The cold-start season. New flagship runs, returning juggernauts, and at least one quiet show that nobody saw coming.
editorial.spring: The patience season. A handful of long-awaited sequels, a few quiet premieres, and at least one title that will be remembered.
editorial.summer: The bright-noise season. Big swings, louder palettes, and the kind of debuts that thrive on word of mouth.
editorial.fall: The reckoning season. Awards bait, finale-heavy continuations, and the year's most ambitious one-cours.
editorial.all: The full year in one frame. Premieres, sequels, and finales — every title of the year, in review.
